thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Higher, Buoyed by Upbeat Earnings, Outlook from Apple

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Higher, Buoyed by Upbeat Earnings, Outlook from Apple
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Wednesday's regular session:
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.9%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): +0.1%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): +0.07%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): +0.2%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): -1.5%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV edged lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was up 0.2%.
US stock futures were modestly higher ahead of the open, buoyed by Apple (AAPL) as the iPhone maker's Q3 financial results and outlook for Q4 beat Street estimates.
Traders are also focused on a fresh set of data, and looking ahead to the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision later in the session.
The private sector added 219,000 jobs for July, according to Automated Data Processing -- the highest increase in payrolls since February. Forecasts had called for a 173,000 increase. The June figure was revised to 181,000 from the initial figure of 177,000.
The PMI manufacturing index, out at 9:45 am ET, is expected to come in at a final 55.5 in July, from previous level of 55.4.
The Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing index, to be reported at 10 am ET, is expected to come in 59.5 for July versus the prior level of 60.2. Construction spending is seen rising 0.3% in June versus May's 0.4% rise.
And at 2 pm ET, the Federal Open Market Committee is expected to keep its federal funds target range at 1.75% to 2% for a 1.875% implied target.
Power Play: Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was up 0.01% and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) rose some 5% after it reported Q3 sales of $53.26 billion, up from $45.4 billion in the year ago quarter and better than the analyst consensus of $52.4 billion on Capital IQ. Earnings were $2.34 per share, up from $1.67 per share a year ago and topping estimates of $2.18 per share. For Q4, the company is targeting revenue in the range of $60 to $62 billion, vs. expectations of $59.4 billion. In Q3, the company sold 41.3 million iPhones, up slightly from the 41 million sold a year ago. iPad sales were 11.5 million units vs. 11.42 million last year. Mac sales were 3.7 million units vs. 4.29 million units a year ago. Services revenue was 9.54 billion, up from $7.26 billion last year.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.2%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) were inactive in the pre-market session.
Ares Capital (ARCC) rose 0.6% after it reported Q1 core EPS of $0.39, versus $0.32 last year. This beat the $0.38 Street view. Portfolio investments at fair value were $12.20 billion, versus $11.41 billion last year. Ares reported revenue of $317 million for the period, versus $275 million in the year-ago period and ahead of the Street view expecting $310 million. The company declared a second quarter dividend of $0.38 per share, payable on June 29, to stockholders of record as of June 15.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.8% in pre-market trade.
Chesapeake Energy (CHK) rose nearly 6% after it reported Q2 adjusted net profit of $0.15 per share, down from $0.18 per share in the prior year period which came in line with the Street estimate provided by Capital IQ. Revenue for the quarter was $982 million, down from $1.28 billion reported for the same period last year. The Street estimate was for revenue of $1.13 billion. For 2018, the company expects total production to range from 180 million to 190 million barrels of oil equivalent, while capital expenditures are expected to reach $2.18 billion to $2.48 billion.
Commodities
Crude was down 1.4%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 1.2%. Natural gas was up 0.1% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.3%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was down 0.1%. Silver was up 0.5%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.5%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were inactive. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was down quiet in pre-market trading .
TrovaGene (TROV) jumped 6% after the company said the European Medicines Agency (EMA) Committee for Orphan Medicinal Products (COMP) has adopted a positive opinion recommending PCM-075 for designation as an orphan medicinal product to treat Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML). The positive opinion issued by the COMP is anticipated to be adopted by the European Commission (EC) at the end of August.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) and retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market trade.
Pandora Media (P) rose nearly 13% after it reported Q2 revenue of $384.8 million, up from $376.8 million in the year ago quarter and ahead of the analyst consensus of $373.5 million on Capital IQ. Non-GAAP loss was $0.15 per share, narrower than the year ago loss of $0.21 per share and the Street view calling for a loss of $0.17 per share.
